To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermal conductivity of liquids and gases is strongly dependent on the temperature and pressure of the substance and that the temperature and pressure dependence is different for different liquids and gases.
the thermal conductivity values of most nonmetallic pure liquids and gases are higher than those of their corresponding solid states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement, compilation, evaluation, and prediction of thermophysical properties of pure substances and mixures.
the measurement and prediction of thermophysical properties of materials.
the measurement and correlation of the thermophysical properties of materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TPRC Data Project represents a monumental achievement.
the TPRC Data series is the most important and valuable collection of thermophysical properties ever published in the scientific literature.
the TPRC Data Project is the most important single source of information on thermophysical properties of matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Data Series has been a success.
this series of volumes provides an extensive and authoritative compilation of thermophysical property data for materials of importance in science and technology.
this Data Series is an important and unique compilation of experimental and recommended data for thermophysical properties of matter, which is of value to the scientific and engineering communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal conductivity of the gas phase is not the limiting factor for the thermal conductivity of gas-liquid systems, as it has been previously thought.
the thermal conductivity of a liquid is strongly influenced by the presence of a solid-liquid interface.
the thermophysical properties of the materials we tested were not significantly different from those of the materials used in the previous study.
